sources.title: A new proof that more than $2/3$ of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v2: Theorem 1.1 and Proposition 2.1; submission history
sources.source_claim: Lamzouri reports unconditional asymptotic proportions above 67.25% for simple critical-line zeros and above 83.62% for distinct zeros. Version 2 adds an 88.76% bound for zeros that are simple OR on the critical line, plus a bound on the average of those two proportions. The mechanism is a Hilbert-space kernel inequality.
sources.limits: The union bound is not an 88.76% critical-line bound. None of these proportions proves RH or full prime-resolvent positivity. Version 2 was posted on 8 September; the first submission was 2 September.
sources.reuse: Bibliographic metadata and original synthesis only; no permission to train on linked full text is inferred.

sources.limits: The useful bound depends on theta and is asymptotic. It is not the global 67.25% bound for every short interval or a certified finite-height zero count.

repository_cards.bridge_hypothesis: Use collision resets to test the distinction between rapid refresh and bounded-cost autonomous maintenance. Dictionary: collision period -> refresh time; first-order support leakage -> coefficient of t log(1/t). A speed limit does not control the ancilla reset work.
repository_cards.next_finite_task: For a rank-deficient qubit target and one leaking jump, compare free-energy loss divided by t with log(1/t). In a collision implementation include the ancilla reset cost and finite refresh error.
repository_cards.falsifier: Reject a finite-power exact-refresh claim if it suppresses the first-order leakage term by changing the target rank or leaves reset work unaccounted.

repository_cards.bridge_hypothesis: Classify the experimental collision protocol before comparing it with additive GKLS no-go results. Dictionary: repeated unitary-plus-reset channel -> a possible continuous-time generator only in a controlled limit. Pulse resources, memory and target purity may change.
repository_cards.next_finite_task: Derive a small collision channel and its candidate generator, check complete positivity and outward support flow, and compare fixed-point error versus reset rate with the existing two-state model.
repository_cards.falsifier: A finite-time channel without a valid additive GKLS limit is outside the theorem class. A mixed target or changing background generator cannot refute the rank-deficient fixed-background no-go.
